result.title: LeHami: Symplectic Latent Dynamics for World Models
result.summary: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn world models directly in latent space, but unconstrained autoregressive predictors may contract the latent distribution over long rollouts. We introduce Symplectic Hamiltonian JEPA (LeHami), which replaces the standard predictor with an action-conditioned Hamiltonian flow over a structured latent state (q, p) integrated using an exactly symplectic leapfrog step. This construction preserves phase-space volume at every rollout step and rules out uniform contraction, asymptotically stable fixed points, and merging of distinct latent states, independently of the learned parameters or action sequence. We obtain the momentum-like component from temporal derivatives of the learned position-like representation, providing an explicit second-order state for prediction and control. On conservative and actuated visual pendulum environments, LeHami substantially improves long-horizon velocity prediction over an unconstrained JEPA world model and empirically maintains constant latent volume where the baseline contracts. The learned flow also supports accurate integration at unseen sub-frame step sizes and numerical time reversal. These results show how geometric structure can provide inference-time guarantees that are complementary to representation regularization in latent world models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 LeHami，用动作条件下的 Hamiltonian 流替换 JEPA 世界模型的普通自回归预测器，在结构化 latent 状态 (q, p) 上以保辛 leapfrog 积分，从而在任意参数与动作下保持相空间体积、排除 latent 收缩与状态合并，并在视觉摆环境中改善长程速度预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「latent 状态在长 rollout 中收缩/不同状态合并」的失效分析与 LVR 中 latent 信息坍缩、多步状态更新的稳定性问题直接对应，保辛结构作为替代表示正则化的推理期约束可供核查；但对象是低维动力学世界模型而非 VLM 推理，迁移性需自行判断。
